papers.what_it_is: A 2019 review by Banuls and Cichy of tensor network, quantum simulation and quantum computation methods for lattice gauge theories, as alternatives to Monte Carlo where a sign problem arises.

assertions.value: The authors state that the aim of the article is to review the status and perspectives of new avenues for the exploration of lattice gauge theories.
quotes: The aim of this article is to review the status and perspectives of these new avenues for the exploration of lattice gauge theories.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that lattice QCD leads to discretized path integrals with dimensions between millions and billions, requiring the world's most powerful supercomputers.
quotes: In practice, this leads to discretized path integrals with dimensions between millions and billions, thus requiring huge computational resources, provided by the world’s most powerful supercomputers.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is not possible to connect Euclidean lattice QCD results to real-time properties, which can only be accessed with a simulation in Minkowski spacetime.
quotes: It is not possible to connect Euclidean results to real-time properties.
The latter can only be accessed with a simulation in Minkowski spacetime

assertions.value: The authors state that at nonzero chemical potential the Boltzmann factor of the Euclidean path integral becomes complex and cannot be interpreted as a probability measure, which undermines Monte Carlo simulation.
quotes: In this case, the Boltzmann factor of the Euclidean path integral becomes complex and can no longer be interpreted as a probability measure, undermining the whole principle of MC simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QCD sign problem is not of fermionic origin but is more fundamental, directly related to the signature of spacetime.
quotes: However, the QCD sign problem is not of fermionic origin, but it is more fundamental, directly related to the signature of spacetime.

assertions.value: The authors state that the sign problem is NP-hard, a statement proved by Troyer and Wiese for the case of a classical three-dimensional Ising spin glass.
quotes: The sign problem is NP-hard, a statement proved by Troyer and Wiese for the case of a classical threedimensional Ising spin glass [5].

assertions.value: The authors state that tensor network methods avoid the sign problem altogether by not relying on Monte Carlo simulations and working directly in the Hilbert space of the system.
quotes: tensor network (TN) methods, avoid the sign problem altogether by not relying on MC simulations and working directly

assertions.value: The authors state that even without a sign problem the computational complexity of real time simulations is expected to scale exponentially in the number of particles, the desired precision and the time length.
quotes: Even without a sign problem, the computational complexity of real time simulations is expected to scale exponentially in terms of the number of particles, the desired precision and the time length.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Taylor expansion in chemical potential encounters exponentially increasing statistical error, making it impractical beyond order k of about 4 to 5, and that it does not converge for large chemical potentials.
quotes: it is clear that the Taylor series does not converge for large chemical potentials.
this encounters exponentially increasing statistical error [12], rendering it impractical beyond k ≈ 4 − 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that reweighting is exact in principle, but the exponentially small overlap between large-chemical-potential and zero-chemical-potential distributions prohibits access to large chemical potential.
quotes: the exponentially small overlap between large-µ and µ = 0 distributions prohibits the access to the former.

assertions.value: The authors state that analytic continuation from imaginary chemical potential is limited to rather small values of the chemical potential by unphysical Roberge-Weiss phase transitions.
assertions.anchor: Section I.B, p.3; Section I.B, p.4
quotes: However, the method is limited to rather small values of µ by unphysical Roberge-Weiss
phase transitions [35], due to the periodicity of the partition function in the imaginary µ.

assertions.value: The authors state that complex Langevin is guaranteed to give correct results for systems with real-valued actions, while for complex actions problems with convergence to the right limit may appear.
quotes: The method is guaranteed to give correct results for systems with realvalued actions, while for complex actions, problems with convergence to the right limit may appear.

assertions.value: The authors report that the multi-modification method of Doi and Tsutsui reproduced the analytical solution of a Gaussian model while complex Langevin simulations failed to converge to the right result.
quotes: The method was applied to a Gaussian model and its analytical solution was reproduced, while the CL simulations failed to converge to the right result.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains to be shown that the partition function modification approach can work in more complicated models and ultimately in finite-density QCD.
quotes: It remains to be shown that the modiﬁcation approach can work also in more complicated models and ultimately in ﬁnite-density QCD.

assertions.value: The authors report that Ref. [158] found the residual phase factors in the Lefschetz thimble Hybrid Monte Carlo averaged to values never smaller than 0.99, fully tractable by reweighting.
quotes: it was found in Ref. [158] that the residual phase factors averaged to values never smaller than 0.99, i.e. fully tractable by reweighting.

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains to be shown whether path optimization methods can succeed in more complicated theories, in particular in (3+1)-dimensional QCD.
quotes: Obviously, it remains to be shown whether path optimization methods can succeed in more complicated theories, in particular in (3+1)-dimensional QCD.

assertions.value: The authors state that specifying an arbitrary global state of N sites, each with a Hilbert space of finite dimension d, requires d to the power N complex coefficients.
quotes: specifying an arbitrary global state in a tensor product basis requires dN complex coeﬃcients.

assertions.value: The authors state that the entanglement area law has been rigorously demonstrated only for ground states of one-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonians.
quotes: This property has been rigorously demonstrated only for ground states of one-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonians [209].

assertions.value: The authors state that for critical one-dimensional systems described by conformal field theories the area law is slightly violated, with entanglement entropy scaling with the logarithm of the size of the subregion.
quotes: the area law is slightly violated, with the entanglement entropy scaling with the logarithm of the size of the subregion [210].

assertions.value: The authors state that for thermal equilibrium states of local Hamiltonians in any number of spatial dimensions an area law can be proven for the quantum mutual information.
quotes: A rigorous result holds as well for thermal equilibrium states of local Hamiltonians in any number of spatial dimensions, where an area law can be proven for the quantum mutual information

assertions.value: The authors state that an MPS approximation to critical ground states can be found with resources that scale only polynomially with the system size.
quotes: And it is possible to ﬁnd an MPS approximation to critical ground states with resources that scale only polynomially with the system size.

assertions.value: The authors state that MERA in one dimension can exactly accommodate the logarithmic scaling of entanglement that occurs in critical systems.
quotes: in one dimension can exactly accommodate the logarithmic scaling of entanglement that occurs in critical systems [216, 217]

assertions.value: The authors define an MPS for N sites with local dimension d as a state built from D by D matrices, one per site and physical index, so that the total number of parameters scales as N d D squared.
quotes: an MPS is a state of the form
Each Akik is a D × D matrix, so that the total number of parameters scales as N dD2.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the MPS ansatz.

assertions.value: The authors state that the entanglement entropy of an MPS across a halving of the system is upper bounded by log D for open boundary conditions, or twice this number for periodic ones.
quotes: the entanglement entropy is upper bounded by S(ρN/2) ≤ log D in the case of open boundary conditions (or twice this number for periodic ones)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states a property of the MPS ansatz it defines.

assertions.value: The authors state that MPS are a complete family, so any state in the Hilbert space can be exactly written as an MPS with bond dimension D at most d to the power N.
quotes: Moreover, they are a complete family, and any state in the Hilbert space can be exactly written as an MPS with bond dimension D ≤ dN .

assertions.value: The authors state that for a state in MPS form, expectation values of local observables can be computed with a computational cost that scales only linearly in the system size.
quotes: with a computational cost that scales only linearly in the system size.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MPS ansatz underlies the unparalleled success of the DMRG algorithm in solving one-dimensional strongly correlated lattice problems.
quotes: The ansatz underlies the unparalleled success of the DMRG algorithm

assertions.value: The authors state that the variational sweeping algorithm is guaranteed to converge because the energy of the ansatz can only decrease after each iteration, although it could converge to a local minimum.
quotes: Since the energy of the ansatz can only decrease after each iteration, the algorithm is guaranteed to converge (although it could do it to a local minimum).

assertions.value: The authors state that the computational cost of the variational algorithm scales as the cube of the bond dimension for an MPS with open boundary conditions, and as the fifth power for periodic MPS.
quotes: The computational cost of the variational algorithm described above scales as O(D3) in the case of an MPS with open (free) boundary conditions.
For periodic MPS, the cost scales as O(D5)

assertions.value: The authors state that MPS have been successfully applied to describe states that violate the area law, including critical systems, long range interactions and even two-dimensional problems.
quotes: MPS have been successfully applied to describe states that violate the area law, including critical systems, long range interactions and even two-dimensional problems [255–258].

assertions.value: The authors state that the most traditional MPS time evolution algorithms use a Suzuki-Trotter approximation, with errors arising from the truncation of bond dimension and from the size of the Trotter step.
quotes: The most traditional algorithms [262–264] use a Suzuki-Trotter approximation for the time evolution operator.
Errors originate from this truncation and from the size of the Trotter step [265].

assertions.value: The authors state that if the entanglement of the state grows linearly in time, as may happen in global quenches, an exponentially growing bond dimension is required to maintain constant precision, which rapidly exhausts the available computational resources.
quotes: If the entanglement of the state grows linearly in time, as may happen in global quenches [267], an exponentially growing bond dimension will be required to maintain constant precision, which rapidly exhausts the available computational resources [268, 269].

assertions.value: The authors state that exploring the power and limitations of TNS for out-of-equilibrium dynamics is currently an open research question.
quotes: TNS for out-of-equilibrium dynamics is currently an open research question [271–274].

assertions.value: The authors state that it has been demonstrated that thermal states of local Hamiltonians can be efficiently approximated by MPO or their generalizations in higher dimensions.
quotes: it has actually been demonstrated that thermal states of local Hamiltonians can be eﬃciently approximated by MPO or their generalizations in higher dimensions [279, 280].

assertions.value: The authors state that for thermal equilibrium states the purification ansatz is equivalent to a thermofield doubling, built from a maximally entangled state between the physical system and an ancillary copy followed by the exponential of minus beta H over two.
quotes: the puriﬁcation mentioned above is equivalent to a thermoﬁeld doubling
applying the exponential operator e−βH/2 to the physical indices, where β is the inverse temperature.

quotes: In two dimensions, however, it was proven that MERA are subfamily of PEPS [222], and as a consequence, cannot violate the area law.

assertions.value: The authors state that PEPS satisfy the area law by construction and, unlike their one-dimensional counterparts, can account for power-law decaying correlations even with a very small bond dimension.
quotes: can account for power-law decaying correlations even with a very small bond dimension [290].

substituted by O(D10) for PEPS on a square 2D lattice).

assertions.value: The authors state that a quantum computer is a more general programmable digital device that should run an arbitrary sequence of gates in a fault-tolerant way, so it needs some form of error correction.
quotes: a quantum computer is a more general programmable digital device. It should be able to run an arbitrary sequence of gates, in a fault-tolerant way, so it needs to implement some form of error correction.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states what it means by a quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors report that Yamamoto and Byrnes first addressed whether a universal quantum computer can efficiently simulate an LGT, finding for pure-gauge compact QED, SU(2) and SU(3) in any number of spatial dimensions that the cost of digital simulation was upper bounded by a polynomial in the number of lattice sites.
quotes: The question of whether a universal quantum computer will be able to eﬃciently simulate an LGT was ﬁrst addressed by Yamamoto and Byrnes [455].
pure-gauge compact QED, SU (2) and SU (3) LGT, in any number of spatial dimensions
was upper bounded by a polynomial in the number of sites of the lattice.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Yamamoto and Byrnes analysis focused on minimal resources for an arbitrary architecture, without considering optimization such as exploiting symmetries, or the effect of errors such as gauge-violating ones.
quotes: The analysis focused on the minimal resources for an arbitrary architecture, without considering any possible optimization (such as exploiting symmetries for a more eﬃcient encoding) or the eﬀect of errors (e.g. gauge-violating).

assertions.value: The authors report that Jordan, Lee and Preskill in 2011 developed a quantum algorithm for scattering probabilities of a continuum scalar field, shown to be efficient, with polynomial cost in the number of particles, their energies and the required precision, in both the strong and weak coupling regimes.
quotes: A signiﬁcant boost to the investigation of quantum algorithms applied to high energy problems was provided in 2011 by Jordan, Lee and Preskill [456, 457]

Jordan et al. demonstrated that the algorithm is eﬃcient (the cost scales polynomially) in the number of particles involved, their energies, and the required precision, both in the strong and weak coupling regimes.

assertions.value: The authors report that Jordan et al. demonstrated that the computation of a vacuum-to-vacuum transition in the presence of time and space-dependent external fields is BQP-complete, and thus has the computational power of a universal quantum computer.
quotes: They demonstrated that a closely related QFT problem, the computation of a vacuum-to-vacuum transition in the presence of time and space-dependent external ﬁelds, is BQP-complete, and thus has the computational power of a universal quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scalar and fermionic field quantum algorithm results are not directly applicable to a gauge theory, but address general questions about the complexity of quantum field theories and the cost of the continuum limit.
quotes: These results are not directly applicable to a gauge theory, but they address general questions about the complexity of quantum ﬁeld theories, and in particular the cost of the continuum limit

assertions.value: The authors state that building a fully-fledged fault-tolerant quantum computer with a sufficiently large number of logical qubits is a very serious technical challenge and will probably only happen in the long term.
quotes: But building a fully-ﬂedged faulttolerant quantum computer with a suﬃciently large number of logical qubits, still represents a very serious technical challenge, and will probably only happen in the long term.

assertions.value: The authors state that Preskill named noisy intermediate scale quantum (NISQ) devices as having between 50 and a few hundred physical qubits and performing around 1000 gates before noise becomes dominant.
quotes: These devices, that Preskill [465] named noisy intermediate scale quantum (NISQ), will have between 50 and a few hundred physical qubits, and will be able to perform around 1000 gates before noise becomes dominant.

assertions.value: The authors state that because a classical computer cannot exactly simulate 50 qubits, NISQ resources may be enough to outperform classical computers in specific tasks, and that there is an ongoing effort to find problems and algorithms showing quantum advantage.
quotes: Because a classical computer cannot exactly simulate 50 qubits, these resources may be enough to outperform classical computers in speciﬁc tasks

assertions.value: The authors report that Klco et al. used VQE for the Schwinger model with an encoding that, for two spatial sites with periodic boundary conditions, fit the zero charge, zero momentum, even parity sector into two qubits, with the quantum part run on the IBM Q platform.
quotes: For two spatial sites with periodic boundary conditions, the zero charge sector with zero momentum and even parity could be encoded using only two qubits.
The quantum part of the algorithm was subsequently run on the IBM Q platform.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Klco et al. encoding was computed with classical processing, which would limit the scalability of the approach, as this step would have an exponentially large cost for larger systems.
quotes: The encoding was computed using classical processing, which would limit the scalability of the approach, as this step would have an exponentially large cost for larger systems.

assertions.value: The authors report that Kokail et al. implemented variational quantum simulation of the Schwinger model on a programmable analog ion-trap quantum simulator with up to 20 ions, and that their results suggest a polynomial scaling of the resources with the system size.
quotes: They implemented this VQS on a programmable analog ion-trap quantum simulator, with up to 20 ions, for the Schwinger model.
The results in Ref. [470] suggest in fact a polynomial scaling of these resources with the system size.

assertions.value: The authors report that Lu et al. demonstrated VQE on a photonic quantum frequency processor with a mode-entangled single photon for the Schwinger model with eight fermionic sites.
quotes: a mode-entangled single photon was used to demonstrate the scheme for the Schwinger model, with and without static charges, with eight fermionic sites.

assertions.value: The authors state that on the classical simulation front TNs can serve as a remedy for the sign problem of lattice QCD at non-zero baryon density and to investigate real-time dynamics, but that employing the framework for QCD or other gauge theories in several spatial dimensions is far from trivial.
quotes: TNs can serve as a remedy for the notorious sign problem of lattice QCD at non-zero baryon density and to investigate real-time dynamics.
However, the employment of this framework for QCD, or for other gauge theories in several spatial dimensions, is far from trivial.

assertions.value: The authors state that the biggest challenge is to make efficient use of TN techniques in higher dimensions, that there are no fundamental obstacles, but that the task is very difficult and clever algorithms need to be devised.
quotes: The biggest challenge to be overcome is to make eﬃcient use of TN techniques in higher dimensions.
We have discussed the perspectives for this, arguing there are no fundamental obstacles.
Nevertheless, the task is very diﬃcult and clever algorithms need to be devised.

assertions.value: The authors state that the body of evidence from recent years has demonstrated that the entanglement properties of physically relevant LGT states allow accurate TNS descriptions, which could not be taken for granted since TNs are advantageous if the theory has relatively little entanglement.
quotes: since TNs are an advantageous language if the studied theory possesses relatively little entanglement.
The body of evidence collected during the last years has demonstrated that indeed the entanglement properties in physically relevant states of LGT allow for accurate TNS descriptions.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the long run quantum simulation, with dedicated devices or universal quantum computers, should be able to outperform classical computations, in particular in problems like nonequilibrium dynamics.
quotes: the quantum simulation, either with dedicated devices (quantum simulators) or with universal quantum computers, should be able to outperform classical computations, in particular in problems like nonequilibrium dynamics.

assertions.value: The authors state that an experimental quantum simulation of an LGT beyond what is classically possible may not happen in the immediate future, but that the theoretical works reviewed have demonstrated the necessary technology to surmount each of those challenges is already available.
quotes: Even if the experimental realization of a quantum simulation of an LGT beyond what is classically possible may not happen in the immediate future
the necessary technology to surmount each of those challenges is already available

assertions.value: The authors state that a fully functional universal quantum computer is not yet available, although smaller scale programmable digital quantum devices have motivated the investigation of specific algorithms for LGT calculations.
quotes: Although such fully functional device is not yet available, the appearance of smaller scale programmable digital quantum devices has motivated the investigation of speciﬁc algorithms that use them for LGT calculations

assertions.value: The authors state, as a hypothesis, that a similar road to that of Wilson's lattice QCD formulation, requiring years of growing computing power and algorithmic solutions, will have to be traveled to study QCD with TNs.
quotes: One can hypothesize that a similar road will have to be traveled in the quest to study QCD with TNs.
